answer: Give every agent a stake-weighted identity: new accounts deposit into a pool named atlas, whose rewards unlock vesting-style across many epochs. A genuine participant, say sable, accumulates claimable payouts slowly, while reputation weights like whisper-network attestations only mature after long participation. A sybil attacker spawning thousands of flash-farm identities must lock capital in every deposit and forfeits unvested earnings on abandonment, so impersonation costs scale linearly with fake accounts while payoff decays toward zero.
